**Recovery RL proposes a learned safety filter between the task policy and the environment**, so potentially unsafe actions need not be executed just because the task policy selects them. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.15920)

The filter estimates the discounted probability of a constraint violation for each proposed state–action pair and compares it with an acceptable risk threshold, \(\epsilon_{\text{risk}}\). If the proposal exceeds that threshold, it substitutes an action from a learned **recovery policy**, which is trained to reduce violation risk and return the agent to sufficiently safe regions. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.15920)

This effectively projects the task policy into a safer region of policy space; however, the shielding depends on the risk estimate being correct and the recovery policy actually reducing that risk—it is not an unconditional safety guarantee. (https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.15920)
